plan.title: Amazing Apples
plan.weeklyOverview: This week, toddlers will explore the wonderful world of apples through hands-on investigations, sensory experiences, movement, music, dramatic play, art, and early science activities. Children will discover that apples come in different colors, sizes, and tastes while learning where apples grow and how they become healthy foods we can enjoy. Throughout the week, they will strengthen language skills, early math concepts, fine and gross motor development, and social-emotional skills by working together during engaging apple-themed experiences.
plan.objectives:
Identify apples as a healthy fruit.
Recognize red, green, and yellow apples.
Explore apples using the five senses.
Compare apples by size, color, and texture.
Practice counting, sorting, and matching apples.
Strengthen fine motor skills through art and sensory play.
Build vocabulary related to apples and orchards.
Encourage curiosity through simple science investigations.
Participate in cooperative play and group discussions.
Develop confidence while exploring new foods and experiences.

plan.familyConnection: Invite families to visit a grocery store or orchard together to look for different apples. Encourage children to taste apples at home and talk about their favorite color, taste, and texture.
plan.observationOpportunities:
Color recognition
Counting skills
Vocabulary development
Sensory exploration

Social interactions

plan.adaptations:
Provide adaptive scissors and crayons as needed.
Use picture cards for vocabulary support.
Offer larger manipulatives for children needing additional assistance.
Modify activities based on developmental levels.

items.title: Apple Investigation
items.objective: Introduce children to observing apples using their five senses.
items.description: Children investigate real apples by looking, touching, smelling, and listening while learning descriptive vocabulary.
items.materials:
Red, green, and yellow apples
hand lenses
items.setup: Place apples in the center of the table with hand lenses nearby.
items.steps:
1. Give each child an apple.
2. Look closely using hand lenses.
3. Feel the smooth skin.
4. Smell the apple.
5. Tap gently and listen to the sound.
6. Talk about what everyone noticed.
items.teacherRole: Encourage observation by asking open-ended questions and introducing new vocabulary.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's willingness to explore and describe the apples.
items.adaptations: Provide larger apples or additional teacher support as needed.
items.safetyNotes: Closely supervise children while handling real apples.

items.title: Apple Stamp Painting
items.objective: Explore color while creating apple artwork.
items.description: Children use apple halves dipped in paint to create colorful apple prints.
items.materials:
Apple halves
Red, green, and yellow paint
White construction paper
Smocks
items.setup: Cut apples in half before the activity and pour paint into shallow trays.
items.steps:
1. Dip the apple into paint.
2. Press onto paper.
3. Lift carefully.
4. Repeat using different colors.
5. Allow artwork to dry for display.
items.teacherRole: Model stamping techniques and encourage color recognition.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe hand control and participation.
items.adaptations: Provide sponge stamps if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use only non-toxic washable paint and supervise closely.

items.title: Count the Apples
items.objective: Practice one-to-one counting.
items.description: Children count plastic apples and place them into baskets.
items.materials:
Plastic apples
Small baskets
Number cards 1–5
items.setup: Place apples beside empty baskets.
items.steps:
1. Choose a number card.
2. Count the correct number of apples.
3. Place apples into the basket.
4. Count together.
5. Repeat with another number.
items.teacherRole: Model counting slowly and encourage children to touch each apple as they count.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe counting accuracy and participation.
items.adaptations: Reduce the number of apples or provide hand-over-hand assistance.
items.safetyNotes: Use large manipulatives to prevent mouthing risks.

items.title: Pick the Apples
items.objective: Develop gross motor skills while reinforcing apple vocabulary.
items.description: Children pretend to reach high into an apple tree, pick apples, place them in baskets, and carry them to the pretend orchard.
items.materials:
Music player
Apple baskets
Plastic apples
items.setup: Scatter plastic apples around the classroom.
items.steps:
1. Play apple-themed music.
2. Pretend to reach high into the tree.
3. Pick an apple.
4. Carry it to the basket.
5. Repeat until all apples have been collected.
items.teacherRole: Encourage movement, counting, and imaginative play.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, coordination, and participation.
items.adaptations: Place apples within easy reach or allow seated participation if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Ensure children walk while carrying apples and keep the activity area free of obstacles.

items.title: Apple Color Sort
items.objective: Develop color recognition and sorting skills.
items.description: Children sort apples into matching colored baskets while practicing color vocabulary.
items.materials:
Plastic apples
Red basket
Green basket
Yellow basket
items.setup: Mix all apples together in one large basket.
items.steps:
1. Show each colored basket.
2. Pick up one apple.
3. Name its color.
4. Place it into the matching basket.
5. Count how many apples are in each basket.
items.teacherRole: Encourage children to say each color aloud while sorting.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to identify and sort colors correctly.
items.adaptations: Use only two colors if children need a simpler activity.
items.safetyNotes: Use large manipulatives appropriate for toddlers.

items.title: Apple Peel Tear Collage
items.objective: Tear and stick paper to build a process apple collage.
items.description: Process collage replacing template tissue craft.
items.materials:
Red and green paper for tearing
Glue sticks
Optional light circle guide
Trays
items.setup: Set trays with paper scraps started with one teacher tear.
items.steps: Children tear and stick. No matching model.
items.teacherRole: Encourage creativity while reinforcing color names.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe color choices and participation.
items.adaptations: Offer larger tissue paper pieces or sponge painting.
items.safetyNotes: Closely supervise glue and art materials.

items.title: Apple Color Dance
items.objective: Reinforce color recognition through movement.
items.description: Children dance while holding colorful scarves. When the music stops, the teacher calls a color and children find the matching apple.
items.materials:
Music player
Color scarves
Plastic apples
items.setup: Scatter apples throughout the room.
items.steps:
1. Dance with scarves.
2. Freeze when the music stops.
3. Listen for a color.
4. Find the matching apple.
5. Repeat with different colors.
items.teacherRole: Encourage movement and celebrate successful color matching.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe listening, coordination, and color identification.
items.adaptations: Reduce the number of colors or provide teacher guidance.
items.safetyNotes: Keep the movement area clear and remind children to walk while finding apples.

items.title: Big or Small?
items.objective: Develop comparison and classification skills.
items.description: Children compare apples by size and sort them into "Big" and "Small" baskets.
items.materials:
Large apples
Small apples
Two baskets
Size labels
items.setup: Mix apples together in one large basket.
items.steps:
1. Show the two baskets.
2. Pick up one apple.
3. Decide if it is big or small.
4. Place it into the correct basket.
5. Count the apples in each basket.
items.teacherRole: Model comparison words and encourage children to explain their thinking.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's ability to compare sizes and classify objects.
items.adaptations: Begin with only two noticeably different sizes before introducing medium apples.
items.safetyNotes: Use age-appropriate apples and supervise closely.

items.title: Apple Measuring Station
items.objective: Introduce simple measurement concepts.
items.description: Children explore how apples can be measured using yarn, measuring tape, or linking cubes.
items.materials:
Apples
Measuring tape
Yarn
Linking cubes
items.setup: Arrange measuring materials on a science table.
items.steps:
1. Choose an apple.
2. Wrap yarn around the apple.
3. Compare the yarn lengths.
4. Count linking cubes if using them.
5. Talk about which apple is bigger.
items.teacherRole: Introduce simple measurement vocabulary while encouraging exploration.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity and understanding of measurement.
items.adaptations: Use only one measuring tool if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Closely supervise measuring materials.

items.title: Roll Like an Apple
items.objective: Develop body awareness and gross motor skills.
items.description: Children pretend to be apples by curling into a ball, rolling carefully on mats, stretching into apple trees, and reaching high to pick pretend apples.
items.materials:
Gym mats
Music player
Bean bags
items.setup: Create a large open movement area with mats.
items.steps:
1. Pretend to grow into an apple tree.
2. Reach up high.
3. Curl into a round apple.
4. Carefully roll across the mat.
5. Stand up and pretend to place your apple into a basket.
items.teacherRole: Model each movement and encourage safe participation.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, coordination, and participation.
items.adaptations: Allow children to perform movements while seated or with teacher assistance.
items.safetyNotes: Use mats on a flat surface and supervise rolling activities closely.

items.title: Apple Taste Test
items.objective: Explore different apple varieties using the sense of taste.
items.description: Children sample small pieces of red, green, and yellow apples while comparing their flavors and textures.
items.materials:
Red apples
Green apples
Yellow apples
Small plates
Napkins
items.setup: Wash and slice apples before children arrive. Place one slice of each apple on every plate.
items.steps:
1. Look at each apple.
2. Smell each apple.
3. Taste one slice at a time.
4. Talk about which apple tastes sweet, tart, or crunchy.
5. Choose your favorite apple.
items.teacherRole: Encourage children to describe what they taste while respecting that everyone may have different preferences.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's willingness to try new foods and describe their experiences.
items.adaptations: Offer only one apple variety if children are hesitant or have sensory sensitivities.
items.safetyNotes: Always check for food allergies. Cut apples into small bite-sized pieces and supervise closely during tasting.

items.title: Favorite Apple Graph
items.objective: Introduce simple graphing and counting skills.
items.description: Children place their name or sticker above their favorite apple color to create a classroom graph.
items.materials:
Large graph paper
Apple color pictures
Name cards or stickers
items.setup: Prepare a graph with three columns labeled Red, Green, and Yellow.
items.steps:
1. Decide your favorite apple.
2. Find the matching column.
3. Place your sticker.
4. Count each column together.
5. Discover which apple was the class favorite.
items.teacherRole: Guide children through counting and comparing which column has the most and least.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe counting skills and ability to interpret simple graphs.
items.adaptations: Use picture cards instead of written names if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Keep graphing materials organized to prevent slipping or clutter.

items.title: Apple Market
items.objective: Encourage imaginative play while practicing social skills.
items.description: Children pretend to buy and sell apples at a classroom farmers market.
items.materials:
Toy cash register
Toy apples
Grocery baskets
Play money
Shopping bags
items.setup: Create a pretend apple market with baskets of apples and a checkout area.
items.steps:
1. Choose to be a shopper or cashier.
2. Pick apples for your basket.
3. Pretend to pay for the apples.
4. Trade roles with a friend.
5. Practice saying "Thank you" and "You're welcome."
items.teacherRole: Model friendly conversations and encourage sharing and turn-taking.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe communication, cooperation, and role-playing skills.
items.adaptations: Provide visual communication cards for children needing language support.
items.safetyNotes: Use only child-safe dramatic play materials.

items.title: Apple Life Cycle
items.objective: Introduce the basic life cycle of an apple.
items.description: Children sequence picture cards showing how apples grow from blossoms into fruit.
items.materials:
Apple life cycle cards
Apple tree poster
Velcro board
items.setup: Arrange the life cycle cards in random order.
items.steps:
1. Look at each picture.
2. Talk about what is happening.
3. Put the pictures in order.
4. Review the sequence together.
5. Repeat as a group.
items.teacherRole: Guide discussion by asking prediction and sequencing questions.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's understanding of simple sequencing and plant growth.
items.adaptations: Reduce the sequence to three pictures if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use large laminated cards appropriate for toddlers.

items.title: Apple Seed Discovery
items.objective: Explore the inside of an apple.
items.description: Children observe an apple cut in half to discover seeds, the core, stem, and flesh while comparing different apples.
items.materials:
Apples
Apple halves
hand lenses
Observation tray
items.setup: Cut apples before the activity and place them on trays.
items.steps:
1. Look inside the apple.
2. Find the seeds.
3. Count the seeds together.
4. Feel the inside of the apple.
5. Compare different apples.
items.teacherRole: Encourage children to ask questions and make observations.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity, counting skills, and descriptive language.
items.adaptations: Use larger visuals if children have difficulty seeing the seeds.
items.safetyNotes: Closely supervise handling of apple pieces and remind children not to place seeds in their mouths.

items.title: My Apple Tree
items.objective: Create an apple tree while reviewing the week's learning.
items.description: Children build an apple tree using handprints, fingerprints, or paper pieces to represent leaves and apples.
items.materials:
Brown construction paper
Green paint
Red pom-poms or fingerprints
Glue
Paper
items.setup: Prepare tree trunks before children arrive.
items.steps:
1. Glue the tree trunk.
2. Add green leaves.
3. Add red apples.
4. Count the apples on your tree.
5. Share your artwork with the class.
items.teacherRole: Encourage children to explain how apples grow on trees.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe creativity, counting, and vocabulary.
items.adaptations: Provide pre-cut tree pieces or sponge painting if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use washable, non-toxic materials.

items.title: Apple Harvest Celebration
items.objective: Celebrate the week's learning through music and movement.
items.description: Children pretend to be apple trees growing from tiny seeds before becoming tall trees filled with apples ready to harvest.
items.materials:
Music player
Plastic apples
Baskets
Scarves
items.setup: Scatter apples around the room and provide baskets.
items.steps:
1. Curl into a tiny seed.
2. Slowly grow into an apple tree.
3. Stretch your branches high.
4. Pick pretend apples.
5. Fill the baskets while dancing to music.
items.teacherRole: Lead movement while reviewing everything learned about apples.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, participation, and understanding of the apple life cycle.
items.adaptations: Allow seated movements or teacher assistance when needed.
items.safetyNotes: Maintain open space for movement and remind children to walk while carrying apples.

items.setup: Prepare a graph with three columns labeled Red, Green, and Yellow.
items.steps:
1. Decide your favorite apple.
2. Find the matching column.
3. Place your sticker.
4. Count each column together.
5. Discover which apple was the class favorite.
items.teacherRole: Guide children through counting and comparing which column has the most and least.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe counting skills and ability to interpret simple graphs.
items.adaptations: Use picture cards instead of written names if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Keep graphing materials organized to prevent slipping or clutter.

items.title: Apple Market
items.objective: Encourage imaginative play while practicing social skills.
items.description: Children pretend to buy and sell apples at a classroom farmers market.
items.materials:
Toy cash register
Toy apples
Grocery baskets
Play money
Shopping bags
items.setup: Create a pretend apple market with baskets of apples and a checkout area.
items.steps:
1. Choose to be a shopper or cashier.
2. Pick apples for your basket.
3. Pretend to pay for the apples.
4. Trade roles with a friend.
5. Practice saying "Thank you" and "You're welcome."
items.teacherRole: Model friendly conversations and encourage sharing and turn-taking.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe communication, cooperation, and role-playing skills.
items.adaptations: Provide visual communication cards for children needing language support.
items.safetyNotes: Use only child-safe dramatic play materials.

items.title: Apple Basket Relay
items.objective: Develop balance and coordination through movement.
items.description: Children carefully carry a pretend apple across the room and place it into a basket before returning to the starting line.
items.materials:
Plastic apples
Small baskets
Music player
Floor markers
items.setup: Place one basket at each end of the activity area.
items.steps:
1. Pick up one apple.
2. Walk carefully to the basket.
3. Place the apple inside.
4. Return to the line.
5. Continue until every apple has been delivered.
items.teacherRole: Encourage careful movement and celebrate teamwork rather than speed.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe balance, body control, and ability to follow directions.
items.adaptations: Reduce the walking distance or allow children to carry lighter objects if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Remind children to walk instead of run and keep pathways clear.

items.title: Apple Life Cycle
items.objective: Introduce the basic life cycle of an apple.
items.description: Children sequence picture cards showing how apples grow from blossoms into fruit.
items.materials:
Apple life cycle cards
Apple tree poster
Velcro board
items.setup: Arrange the life cycle cards in random order.
items.steps:
1. Look at each picture.
2. Talk about what is happening.
3. Put the pictures in order.
4. Review the sequence together.
5. Repeat as a group.
items.teacherRole: Guide discussion by asking prediction and sequencing questions.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe children's understanding of simple sequencing and plant growth.
items.adaptations: Reduce the sequence to three pictures if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use large laminated cards appropriate for toddlers.

items.title: Apple Seed Discovery
items.objective: Explore the inside of an apple.
items.description: Children observe an apple cut in half to discover seeds, the core, stem, and flesh while comparing different apples.
items.materials:
Apples
Apple halves
hand lenses
Observation tray
items.setup: Cut apples before the activity and place them on trays.
items.steps:
1. Look inside the apple.
2. Find the seeds.
3. Count the seeds together.
4. Feel the inside of the apple.
5. Compare different apples.
items.teacherRole: Encourage children to ask questions and make observations.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe curiosity, counting skills, and descriptive language.
items.adaptations: Use larger visuals if children have difficulty seeing the seeds.
items.safetyNotes: Closely supervise handling of apple pieces and remind children not to place seeds in their mouths.

items.title: My Apple Tree
items.objective: Create an apple tree while reviewing the week's learning.
items.description: Children build an apple tree using handprints, fingerprints, or paper pieces to represent leaves and apples.
items.materials:
Brown construction paper
Green paint
Red pom-poms or fingerprints
Glue
Paper
items.setup: Prepare tree trunks before children arrive.
items.steps:
1. Glue the tree trunk.
2. Add green leaves.
3. Add red apples.
4. Count the apples on your tree.
5. Share your artwork with the class.
items.teacherRole: Encourage children to explain how apples grow on trees.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe creativity, counting, and vocabulary.
items.adaptations: Provide pre-cut tree pieces or sponge painting if needed.
items.safetyNotes: Use washable, non-toxic materials.

items.title: Apple Harvest Celebration
items.objective: Celebrate the week's learning through music and movement.
items.description: Children pretend to be apple trees growing from tiny seeds before becoming tall trees filled with apples ready to harvest.
items.materials:
Music player
Plastic apples
Baskets
Scarves
items.setup: Scatter apples around the room and provide baskets.
items.steps:
1. Curl into a tiny seed.
2. Slowly grow into an apple tree.
3. Stretch your branches high.
4. Pick pretend apples.
5. Fill the baskets while dancing to music.
items.teacherRole: Lead movement while reviewing everything learned about apples.
items.observationOpportunities: Observe coordination, participation, and understanding of the apple life cycle.
items.adaptations: Allow seated movements or teacher assistance when needed.
items.safetyNotes: Maintain open space for movement and remind children to walk while carrying apples.

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:monday:ite.imageRequirementReason: Toddlers handle whole apples at the table; the invitation is familiar fruit exploration, not an unusual tray layout.
teacherTips: Offer one whole apple per pair and keep tasting on a separate day so looking stays the focus.
Narrate textures aloud—“cool,” “bumpy stem”—instead of quizzing for color names.

any three whole apples of different skins from the grocery sale bin

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:monday:ite.steps: Invite children into “Apple Stamp Painting”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:monday:ite.setup: Stage materials for “Count the Apples” at one low table or rug spot before inviting children.

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:monday:ite.setup: Stage materials for “Pick the Apples” at one low table or rug spot before inviting children.
cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:monday:ite.steps: Invite children into “Pick the Apples”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

What happens when colors run out in one basket?

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:tuesday:it.steps: Invite children into “Apple Color Sort”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:tuesday:it.steps: Invite children into “Apple Peel Tear Collage”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:tuesday:it.imageRequirementReason: Music-and-scarf movement does not need a photograph.

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:tuesday:it.steps: Invite children into “Apple Color Dance”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:wednesday:.imageRequirementReason: Two baskets with size labels are ordinary classroom sorting.

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:thursday:i.steps: Invite children into “Apple Taste Test”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

cur-lp-toddler-amazing-apples:thursday:i.steps: Invite children into “Favorite Apple Graph”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

week.weeklyOverview: Toddlers explore real apples through looking, sorting, moving, tasting (with allergy care), and process art. Each day adds one new way to know an apple—never the same stamp-and-sort loop twice.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Whole apples (red, green, yellow)
Apple halves for stamping (adult-cut)
Washable paint
Chunky plastic or fabric apples
Baskets and shoebox bins
Dot number cards
Yarn and linking cubes
Scarves
Butcher paper
Glue sticks
Picture card pack (draft PDF)
Napkins and sanitizer
Magnifying tools or view-finders
Gym mats or blankets
week.teacherPreparation: Confirm allergy notes before Thursday tasting. Adult-cut stamp apples Monday morning. Print and cut the Amazing Apples Picture Card Pack. Stage one center fully before children arrive; keep backup props in a closed tub.
week.familyConnection: Ask families to notice an apple at home or store—color, stem, or crunch—and send one word or photo of a grocery apple (no child faces required).
milestones: Language: Uses sensory and color words about apples
SEL: Accepts non-tasting roles during the taste test
Cognition: Sorts by color or size with purpose
Motor: Presses stamps, tears paper, carries baskets
Creativity: Makes process art without a matching model

songs.title: Crunch Goes the Apple (LLH)
songs.rightsEvidence: Original Little Learner Hub chant written for this lesson; not derived from a commercial recording.
songs.lyrics:
Crunch goes the apple, crunch crunch crunch.
I hold it careful—munch munch munch.
Red or green or yellow bright,
I taste my apple—just one bite!
songs.motions: Tap fists together for crunch; mime holding; point to colors; pretend one careful bite.
songs.teacherDirections: Chant slowly before tasting. Offer a silent mouth movement for non-tasters.
songs.whenToUse: Thursday before the taste test and Friday celebration.

songs.title: Way Up High in the Apple Tree
songs.rightsEvidence: Traditional nursery fingerplay widely documented as authorless oral tradition; lyrics appear in public nursery-rhyme collections such as allnurseryrhymes.com/way-up-high-in-the-apple-tree/. Used as a chant/fingerplay in early childhood settings. If a modern recorded arrangement is preferred later, replace with an LLH original.
songs.lyrics:
Way up high in the apple tree,
Two red apples smiled at me.
I shook that tree as hard as I could,
Down came an apple,
Mmm, it was good!
songs.motions: Reach high; smile with hands on cheeks; shake arms; swoop hands down; rub tummy.
songs.teacherDirections: Teach as a spoken fingerplay; melody optional. Change the number each round.
songs.whenToUse: Monday circle and Friday parade warm-up.
songs.transitionPurpose: Connect story language to picking/movement games.

songs.title: Basket Fill (LLH)
songs.rightsEvidence: Original LLH transition chant created for toddler apple sorting and cleanup.
songs.lyrics:
Fill, fill, fill the basket—
Red one, green one, in they go.
Pat the basket, nice and steady,
Apples ready—here we go!
songs.motions: Pretend place apples; pat basket; march two steps.
songs.teacherDirections: Use during cleanup of Count the Apples and Color Sort.

duringReadingPrompts: Can you show me three with your fingers?
